report_summary: A detailed and well-calibrated report reconstructs reciprocal task exchanges, false counter signals, cleanup adaptation, and static versus circumstantial XSS evidence. It explicitly preserves date-only precision, identities versus names, operation denominators and unknown final state. It is substantial prior work for many of the proposed Fide checks.

section_coverage.note: Full narrative, record citations, caveats and conclusions read; assessed through the eight questions below.

attribution.summary: Names and coarse prefixes do not authenticate provider, actor count or maintainer identity; cleanup behavior is distinct from the explicit Friedrich1982 role.

authority.summary: GET-writing is supported by participant recipes and resulting saves, not form_edit alone; an admin-looking namespace and maintainer display name do not establish privilege.

coordination.summary: Reciprocal requests, acknowledgment of a peer lead and later reported same question demonstrate actual information exchange, without independently measured score gains or prohibited collaboration. Accidental counter tests were mistaken for signals and retracted; seed predictions explicitly allowed chance matches.

techniques.summary: Detailed SNI/Host workaround and claimed replications make some bypass success plausible, while actual network responses and policy remain unavailable. The initial static payload has no exact saved-body match; later preference/save coincidences support a linked workflow but do not isolate JavaScript execution.

persistence.summary: Participants described clock manipulation and designed detached beacons, while absent signals did not prove shutdown or successful survival.

impact.summary: Neighboring revisions show actual welcome-page overwrite38seconds after restoration; some other edits preserve original text. CounterAPI overload is participant-reported rather than independently measured. Saves and revisions are duplicate representations, snapshots repeat earlier content, and missing deleted bodies prevent complete creation/loss counts.

recovery.summary: A participant proposed an alphabetically late fallback, created it96seconds later, and both original and backup were subsequently deleted12seconds apart. Recreation and participant-reported archive access plausibly let communication persist during ongoing cleanup.

chronology.summary: Cleanup beginsJune2–4; June20requests have only dayprecision; final retained saveJuly2 and deleteJuly14 do not demonstrate resolution or cause of decline.
